finding.claim: Missing authorization on /admin/drop: the error returned by Authorize(u, "dba") is discarded, so any user (including one with no roles) reaches the DROP TABLE sink.
finding.source: Any HTTP caller routed to dropTable via api.go:44 (/admin/drop)
finding.sink: runSQL call at api.go:27 (protected DDL operation)

trace.note: main registers /admin/drop -> dropTable with no middleware
userFrom(r) loads the user from request context
Authorize(u, "dba") return value ignored; no early return
runSQL executes DROP TABLE regardless of authorization result

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct but its error is dropped at api.go:26. Sibling vacuum (api.go:33-36) checks err and returns 403, so dropTable is the handler missing the check. No middleware in repo. Caveat: whether upstream auth exists is outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. api.go:26 calls Authorize(u, "dba") as a bare statement and discards its error, so there is no early return. Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct but never gates the sink. api.go:44 registers /admin/drop with no middleware, and the repo has no middleware that checks roles. The only other thing on the path is userFrom (api.go:22), which panics if no "user" context value is set. That is a crash, not an authorization control. Nothing in the repo sets that context value, so exploitation depends on upstream auth middleware outside this repo that populates it.
verdict.reason: The check at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error is discarded, so runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 runs for any caller who has a user in context, with no role check, while the sibling vacuum at api.go:33-35 does check and return 403. The finding is confirmed on the code as written, but its reachability depends on upstream auth that populates the "user" context value (api.go:22), which is not in this repo.

finding.claim: SQL injection in /admin/drop: the user-supplied form value t is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement with no quoting, allowlist, or identifier validation.

trace.note: FormValue t concatenated into SQL string and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: No validation of t on this path. Only check is the discarded Authorize call (F1). runSQL is a stub (api.go:41), so multi-statement execution cannot be confirmed from this file.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only control, but its error return is discarded as a bare statement, so it never blocks. No validation, allowlist, or parameterization of t exists on the path to runSQL at api.go:27. The /admin/drop route is registered at api.go:44.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the candidate: the route is at api.go:44, t comes from r.FormValue("t") and is concatenated into "DROP TABLE " + t at api.go:27, and the Authorize result at api.go:26 is discarded, so any caller who gets past userFrom (which requires an authenticated user in context) reaches the concatenation. Caveats: runSQL is a stub at api.go:41, so the actual SQL effect cannot be observed in this file, and the auth middleware that populates the context is not in the provided code.
